source.title: Toward Training at ImageNet Scale with Differential Privacy
source.authors: Alexey Kurakin; Shuang Song; Steve Chien; Roxana Geambasu; A. Terzis; Abhradeep Thakurta

record.file_problem: Full paper text is provided, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates how architecture/model size, training duration, hyperparameters, batch size, and transfer learning affect accuracy under differential privacy on ImageNet and CIFAR-10. These are new settings for the catalog claim, but the outcomes concern privacy-utility rather than the natural-label generalization gap or the listed version-specific measures.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes are mostly test accuracy and privacy loss for differentially private training, including comparisons of model sizes and batch sizes. The paper does not report train-versus-test error gaps or evaluate random-label memorization. Claims about memorization preventing leakage are background motivation, not experiments here.
record.test_reason: Table 7 tests V5 in a new setting: differentially private ImageNet fine-tuning. At fixed epoch budgets and privacy ε = 10, sufficiently large batches reduce held-out accuracy. V5 does not require measuring a train–test gap. Adjusting noise to preserve privacy makes this a comparison of privacy-constrained training recipes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: combining public-data pretraining and selected DP-SGD settings achieves 47.9% ImageNet accuracy at ε = 10 and δ = 10^-6, substantially improving naive private training while remaining below non-private performance. The abstract's approximately 75% comparator is inconsistent with Table 3, which reports 70.8% for ResNet-18 and 75.3% for ResNet-50 at 90 epochs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses differentially private SGD, privacy accounting, and public-data pretraining to study utility under privacy constraints; the cited generalization studies and methods are not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: Under DP training, accuracy varies with model size and privacy level, training duration, clipping norm and learning rate, batch size and number of epochs, and the number of frozen blocks. The authors report that increasing batch size helps only up to a point in the transfer-learning setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller image models can outperform larger models under stronger differential privacy, reversing their non-private ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture size interacts with differential-privacy noise: larger image models need not achieve better held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly scaling batch size, epochs, and noise can maintain approximately similar accuracy while improving the privacy bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed update counts and noise-to-batch ratio, larger-batch DP-SGD can improve privacy at similar utility.

record.problems: The paper describes the work as an initial exploration and says many more explorations remain. Several settings are selected through hyperparameter sweeps; tuning is acknowledged not to preserve privacy. Some reported comparisons show test accuracy and privacy budgets without train accuracy or generalization gaps. Figure 1's main-body values are plotted, with detailed values supplied in Appendix C.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the paper's reported outcomes concern DP utility, accuracy, and privacy loss, rather than the behaviors measured by the claim versions. Numerical test-accuracy comparisons in Tables 4–12 and Figure 6 therefore do not qualify as rows for these versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold; no interpolation threshold or training-error measurements are reported.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Language models; isolation of batch-size effects with noise held constant; whether longer training fully closes the penalty; controlled comparisons of learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization remedies.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Add V5 rows for fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons in Table 7. The blanket exclusion in rows_left_out is incorrect: held-out accuracy at fixed epoch budgets directly measures V5. Record frozen groups, epochs, batch size, ε = 10, learning-rate tuning, and the varying noise multiplier.

Add V5 rows for the fixed-epoch comparisons in Table 9, also incorrectly excluded. At 10 epochs, accuracy declines from 56% at batch 1,024 to 35.5% at 4,096 and 5.8% at 16,384. Record that learning rate is fixed at 16 and noise scales with batch size, so privacy also changes.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to relink. Missing entries correct explicitly declared but erroneous exclusions. Table 7 supports a batch-size penalty under a fixed privacy constraint; it does not isolate batch size from the accompanying noise adjustment. Moderate batch increases improving accuracy are consistent with V5's workload-dependent threshold.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or test-error sweep around zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison on image tasks.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison on the listed image or language benchmarks.
Batch-size outcomes are measured for DP privacy-utility, not the natural-label generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets as stated in this version.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-gap measure.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

relationships.condition: Places365-pretrained ResNet-18 fine-tuned on ImageNet with DP-SGD, ε = 10, fixed epoch budgets, and either three or four frozen block groups.
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict; no extracted row ids exist. Table 7 shows accuracy falling beyond a workload-dependent batch size: with three frozen groups and 70 epochs, accuracy falls from 47.9% at batch 65,536 to 18.4% at batch 1,048,576; with four frozen groups it falls from 38.1% at batch 262,144 to 34.7% at batch 1,048,576.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy declined beyond the batch sizes that gave the best accuracy under fixed epoch budgets, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
